exitCriterion: existing documents above the Expert cap are zero or explicitly migrated, and 201 tokenOverrides produce one named fail-closed result

censusRanFirst.law: the contract requires the census BEFORE the fix — a fail-closed gate landed without knowing what it would reject is a blind change
censusRanFirst.result: no document in the repository exceeds the cap
censusRanFirst.rulingOut: the torture and themanagementmiami brand themes use the fully typed BrandTheme shape and carry no raw tokenOverrides; the brand-studio file export emits a fixed ~20-25 token set and is structurally incapable of approaching the cap

theDefect.before: if (count >= MAX_TOKEN_OVERRIDES) break; — entries past the bound were dropped in enumeration order with no error, no log and no return signal, and the function returned normally as if nothing had happened
theDefect.siblingThatAlreadyFailedClosed: the skin-pack path throws a plain Error naming both the actual count and the bound, and is called at the start of register/apply/acquire so nothing is stored when it throws

theArchitecturalFactBehindIt.budgetAuthority: schemas/tenant-theme/index.ts:1511, inside a frozen limits object whose own comment states that a second literal 200 anywhere is a cascade-integrity defect
theArchitecturalFactBehindIt.consequence: a fully schema-legal document authoring more than 200 of its 294 legally allowlisted tokens passed validateTenantThemeDocument cleanly and was then silently truncated by the compiler. This is reachable by an in-spec author, not an abuse case.
theArchitecturalFactBehindIt.reconciliationLaw: NOT by widening the cap. 294 is the vocabulary and 200 is the budget — structurally distinct mechanisms, allowlist membership versus entry count. The cap was not moved and remains declared in exactly one place.
theArchitecturalFactBehindIt.alsoOnTheCanonicalPath: compileTenantThemeConfig passes its schema-validated normalizedAppearance into the same truncating function, so this was never confined to a legacy compatibility path

documentValidation.change: emits one named issue at $.visualFoundation.advanced.tokenOverrides whose message names both the bound and the actual count
documentValidation.whyThere: validateEnvelopeShape already enforced every OTHER member of the same frozen limits object — maxDepth, maxObjectFields, maxDocumentBytes. maxTokenOverrides was the only limit never checked there; that absence was the root.

compiler.change: rejects over-budget input with a named error quoting the actual count and the bound, matching the skin-pack house pattern, instead of breaking out of the loop

testsRespecifiedNotDeleted.obsolete: appearance.test.ts asserted the truncation as CORRECT — it built cap+25 entries and asserted exactly 200 survived. That test encoded the defect being fixed, so it was respecified rather than removed.
testsRespecifiedNotDeleted.coverageGapClosed: the canonical compileTenantThemeConfig path had no test building a >200 tokenOverrides document. It now has a 201 rejection test and a 200 boundary test, mirroring the three-part shape the skin-pack tests already use: over-cap rejects with a named error, the exact boundary does not, and the bound is read from the schema authority rather than hardcoded.

digestSentinels.law: a silent re-baseline is forbidden; a moved digest must be reported before it is re-anchored
digestSentinels.result: unchanged — TENANT_THEME_DOCUMENT_SCHEMA_DIGEST and TENANT_THEME_CONFIG_SCHEMA_DIGEST were not re-anchored, because adding a check does not alter the schema shape

The authority on this episode is receipts/incident-inherited-worktree-revert.json.
outOfScopeFlagRaisedAndWithdrawn.whatWasFlagged: the removal of the --ds-motion-ambient emission from appearancePostureToVariables, reasoning that a keyword custom property had no productive CSS reader
outOfScopeFlagRaisedAndWithdrawn.whoAuthoredIt: NOT this lane, and no lane in this round. The change was INHERITED from a prior session and arrived with the 161 inherited porcelain entries, carrying a ledger note describing it as a previously reconciled decision. The original text of this block attributing it to the lane was a misattribution.
whyEachRejectionReasonDidNotHold: 'it sat outside the lane's writeSet' — moot: the lane did not make the change, so there was no scope breach to judge

'it removed a capability without census, successor and death proof' — overstated. Per the incident receipt's howTheErrorHappened.compoundingError, the capability survived; only the CSS custom property was withdrawn, with the policy moving to the layer MotionProvider consumes. That is materially different from a capability removed without a successor

'the R1 tenant migration plan has The Management authoring ambient: off' — true that the plan item exists, but it does not support the revert: the plan authors ambient in the DOCUMENT layer, not through the CSS emission that was withdrawn
outOfScopeFlagRaisedAndWithdrawn.howItWasDetected: it changed the compiled artifact CSS relative to the HEAD-pinned digests, which is why three assertions in canonical-digest-identity.test.ts fail against the inherited state
outOfScopeFlagRaisedAndWithdrawn.resolutionAtRoundClose: the revert was itself undone before round close and the inherited state is present in the working tree. The three canonical-digest assertions therefore stand at RED — that is the expected consequence of preserving inherited work that is ahead of the HEAD pins, and no digest was re-anchored in either direction. The earlier claim in this block that the assertions 'returned to green' described the transient reverted state and is false at round close.
outOfScopeFlagRaisedAndWithdrawn.theDesignIsEncodedInTheTree: the earlier claim that 'the rejected design is not encoded anywhere' is false at round close. appearance.test.ts carries the inherited assertion that --ds-motion-ambient is undefined, and appearance-posture/index.ts carries the inherited comment instead of the emission. That is the preserved inherited state, not a landed decision by this round.
outOfScopeFlagRaisedAndWithdrawn.findingPreserved: the underlying observation — that a keyword custom property can be misused in a <time> position — remains an open, un-censused architectural question, recorded for Codex as needing a consumer census rather than settled here
